actions.action: Push a finger 2-3 inches into the soil to check moisture
Tip the plant out of the metal planter and inspect the roots
If roots are mushy, brown or smelly, trim them with clean scissors
Repot into a pot with drainage holes using a chunky aroid mix (bark, perlite, peat/coco)
Alternatively, set the nursery pot inside the decorative planter and empty any collected water
Water thoroughly when the top 2-3 inches are dry and empty the saucer
Move the plant to bright, indirect light
Cut off leaves that are mostly brown

reason: The answer correctly identifies wet soil and poor drainage but misses insufficient light as a cause; still, its main advice (repot into a draining pot with chunky aroid mix and bright light) matches the fix that worked, and nothing it recommends is harmful.
